outputs.L2: Disclosed are kits, devices, assemblies, and techniques for attaching sighting equipment. The sighting device has a base configured to join the device to an object at a first connection interface, a mounting component joined to the base at a second connection interface, and a sighting component attached to the mounting component. A groove formed in the underside of the base is positioned in alignment with a corresponding groove in the object’s surface, and an insert is fastened inside both grooves to firmly attach the sighting device to the object. This firm attachment may prevent the sighting device from shifting relative to the object in at least one direction. The sighting component includes a transparent or non-opaque body that presents a reticle. A lighting component illuminates the reticle from behind from a first viewing position. In some versions, the device also includes an opaque mounting body and a magnifying optical element arranged in line with the sighting component in an open-sight configuration.
outputs.L3:
Kits, apparatus, assemblies, and methods are disclosed for mounting sighting devices to an object. The disclosed configurations may be used to provide a secure, stable connection between a sighting device and an associated object, such as a tool, implement, weapon, support structure, or other item for which alignment, aiming, or visual reference is desired.

In one example, the sighting device includes a base, a mounting element connected to the base, and a sighting element connected to the mounting element. The base may be configured to interface with a corresponding surface or portion of the object. The mounting element may extend from or otherwise attach to the base and may support the sighting element in a desired position relative to the object. The sighting element may provide a visual reference that assists a user in aligning the object with a target, point, path, or other reference location.

To secure the sighting device to the object, the base and the object may include respective channels that are aligned when the base is positioned on the object. A channel insert may be received within the aligned channels and secured therein. By occupying the aligned channels, the channel insert couples the sighting device to the object and helps maintain the relative position of the base with respect to the object.

The resulting connection may be configured to resist movement of the sighting device relative to the object in at least one direction. For example, the channel insert may mechanically interfere with separation, sliding, shifting, rotation, or other displacement of the base relative to the object. In some arrangements, the channel insert may provide resistance in multiple directions, thereby improving the stability and repeatability of the mounted sighting device.

The sighting element may include a non-opaque body that displays a reticle. The reticle may be formed on, within, or otherwise associated with the non-opaque body so that a user can view the reticle while looking through or toward the sighting element. In some embodiments, the reticle may be backlit to improve visibility in low-light conditions or against visually complex backgrounds. The sighting element may also include optional opaque mounting components that support or frame the non-opaque body, as well as optional magnifying optic components configured to enlarge or enhance the viewed image or reticle. Together, these components may provide a durable, accurately mounted sighting device suitable for a variety of alignment and aiming applications.
outputs.L4:
A sighting device mounting system is disclosed for securely attaching a sighting device to an object, such as a firearm, bow, tool, rail, frame, or other support structure requiring accurate visual alignment. The system includes a base associated with the sighting device and an object to which the sighting device is to be mounted. The base and the object each include a channel, groove, slot, recess, or similar receiving feature. When the sighting device is positioned on the object, the channel of the base is aligned with the channel of the object to form a combined passage or receiving region.

A channel insert is positioned within the aligned channels to couple the base to the object. The channel insert may be configured as a key, pin, bar, wedge, spline, dovetail member, or other retaining element shaped to engage both channels simultaneously. Once installed, the channel insert resists relative movement between the sighting device and the object. In particular, the insert may resist sliding, shifting, rocking, rotational movement, lateral displacement, or loosening caused by recoil, vibration, impact, handling, or repeated use. The channel insert may be secured by friction fit, threaded fasteners, set screws, clamping pressure, adhesive, detents, locking features, or any other suitable retention mechanism.

The sighting device may include an open-sight configuration having a non-opaque reticle sighting element. The reticle sighting element may be transparent, translucent, light-transmissive, or otherwise non-opaque so that a user can view a target through or around the reticle while maintaining a visible aiming reference. The reticle may include a dot, ring, crosshair, post, chevron, line, aperture, or other aiming mark. Because the reticle sighting element is non-opaque, the sight picture may remain open and unobstructed, allowing rapid target acquisition and improved situational awareness.

In some embodiments, the sighting device includes an illumination source configured to illuminate the reticle or a portion of the sighting element. The illumination source may include an LED, fiber-optic element, tritium element, electroluminescent component, reflective light collector, or another light-generating or light-directing structure. The illumination may improve visibility of the reticle in low-light conditions, against dark backgrounds, or during rapid aiming. The illumination may be adjustable, selectively activated, battery powered, passively powered, or configured for automatic brightness response.

The sighting device may further include an opaque mounting body that supports the non-opaque reticle sighting element. The opaque mounting body may define the structural portion of the sight and may shield, protect, or frame the reticle. The body may be formed from metal, polymer, composite material, or another rigid material suitable for maintaining alignment under operating conditions. The mounting body may also carry the base portion having the channel that receives the channel insert.

In certain embodiments, the sighting device includes a magnifying optic positioned in optical alignment with the reticle sighting element. The magnifying optic may include a lens or lens assembly configured to enlarge a target image, the reticle, or both. The magnifying optic may be fixed or removable, and may be integrated with the sighting device or used as an attachment. The combination of a non-opaque reticle, optional illumination, and magnification may provide an open-sight system that supports both close-range rapid acquisition and enhanced precision at greater distances.

The mounting system improves the stability and reliability of the sighting device by using the aligned channels and the secured channel insert to create a mechanical interlock between the base and the object. This interlock helps maintain the position and alignment of the sighting device relative to the object even when subjected to recoil, shock, vibration, or repeated adjustment. As a result, the sighting device is less likely to loosen, shift, or lose zero during use.

Accordingly, the disclosed system provides a stable, repeatable, and durable mounting arrangement for sighting devices while also supporting illuminated, non-opaque, and magnified open-sight configurations. The channel insert coupling arrangement enhances mounting strength and alignment retention, and the sighting components provide a clear aiming reference suitable for a variety of operating environments.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the disclosed kits, apparatus, assemblies, and methods for mounting an open sight device to an object using aligned channels and a channel insert.
counterfactuals.output:
The disclosure describes kits, apparatus, assemblies, and methods for mounting an open sight device—such as an iron sight, reflex sight, or other non-telescopic sight—to an object, such as a firearm, bow, tool, or other support structure, using mating channels and a channel insert.

In general, the mounting system includes:

- An open sight device having a first channel or slot.
- An object or mounting base having a second channel or slot.
- A channel insert sized and shaped to be received at least partly in both channels when the channels are aligned.
- One or more fasteners, clamps, pins, screws, or locking members for securing the insert and sight in place.

To mount the sight, the channel of the sight is aligned with the corresponding channel of the object. The channel insert is then placed into the aligned channels so that it bridges or occupies both channels. This insert mechanically couples the sight to the object and helps establish the position, orientation, and stability of the sight. A fastener or retaining mechanism may then be tightened or engaged to prevent movement of the insert and to secure the open sight device against the object.

The disclosed assemblies may provide repeatable alignment, improved resistance to recoil or impact forces, simplified installation, and the ability to remove and reinstall the sight while maintaining its position. The channel insert may be configured to fit dovetail-shaped, rectangular, T-shaped, or other complementary channel geometries. The system may also include adjustment features, such as lateral or vertical positioning elements, to allow the sight to be zeroed or aligned with the object.

The methods generally include:

1. Providing an object with a mounting channel.
2. Providing an open sight device with a corresponding channel.
3. Positioning the sight so that the two channels are aligned.
4. Inserting a channel insert into the aligned channels.
5. Securing the insert and sight using a fastener or locking structure.
6. Optionally adjusting the sight position before final tightening.

The kits may include the open sight device, the channel insert, mounting hardware, and instructions for aligning the channels and securing the sight to the object. Overall, the disclosure is directed to a modular mounting arrangement in which the aligned channels and shared insert provide a secure, repeatable connection between an open sight and the object on which it is mounted.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a technical patent summary for an illuminated open sight assembly with a non-opaque reticle element, opaque mounting body, and secure channel-based attachment interface.
counterfactuals.output:
## Technical Patent Summary: Illuminated Open Sight Assembly with Non-Opaque Reticle Element and Channel-Based Attachment Interface

### Field of the Invention  
The invention relates generally to sighting devices for firearms, archery equipment, air guns, training devices, or other projectile-launching platforms. More particularly, the invention concerns an illuminated open sight assembly having a light-transmissive or non-opaque reticle element supported by an opaque mounting body and secured through a channel-based mechanical attachment interface.

### Background  
Conventional open sights typically rely on non-illuminated posts, beads, notches, or fiber-optic inserts. While such sights may be simple and rugged, they can be difficult to acquire under low-light, high-contrast, or rapidly changing lighting conditions. Some illuminated sight systems use powered emitters, tritium elements, or fiber-optic collectors, but these systems may require complex housings, exposed components, or attachment arrangements that are vulnerable to shock, recoil, impact, or environmental contamination.

In many open sight designs, the aiming reference is formed by an opaque structure. Such structures may obscure portions of the target or surrounding field of view. Conversely, transparent or translucent aiming elements may improve target visibility but can be difficult to mount securely without interfering with illumination or sight picture clarity.

Accordingly, there is a need for an illuminated open sight assembly that provides a visible aiming reference while preserving a field of view, protects or stabilizes the reticle element, and includes a robust attachment interface suitable for repeated shock and field use.

### Summary of the Invention  
The disclosed illuminated open sight assembly includes a non-opaque reticle element mounted to an opaque mounting body. The non-opaque reticle element may be transparent, translucent, light-transmissive, fluorescent, light-guiding, or otherwise configured to convey or emit visible illumination to define an aiming reference. The opaque mounting body provides structural support, blocks stray light, frames the reticle element, and defines a secure channel-based attachment interface.

In one embodiment, the reticle element includes a reticle body received at least partially within a channel of the mounting body. The channel may include opposing sidewalls, undercuts, rails, grooves, shoulders, lips, dovetail surfaces, tapered surfaces, or other retention features that mechanically capture the reticle element. The channel-based interface resists displacement of the reticle element caused by recoil, vibration, impact, thermal cycling, or handling.

The sight assembly may be configured as a front sight, rear sight, auxiliary sight, backup sight, reflex-compatible open sight, or modular sight insert. The reticle element may define an aiming dot, ring, post, bead, triangle, chevron, crosshair, aperture outline, vertical reference, horizontal reference, or other aiming indicia. Illumination may be provided by ambient light collection, a fiber-optic path, photoluminescent material, tritium, an LED, or a combination thereof.

### Principal Components  

#### 1. Non-Opaque Reticle Element  
The reticle element is at least partially non-opaque and may be formed from glass, polymer, acrylic, polycarbonate, optical resin, sapphire, ceramic, fiber-optic material, or another light-transmissive material. The reticle element may include one or more of:

- A transparent or translucent reticle body  
- An illuminated aiming mark formed by geometry, surface treatment, embedded pigment, or internal reflection  
- A light-receiving region for collecting ambient or artificial light  
- A light-emitting region visible to the user  
- A masked, etched, polished, frosted, colored, coated, or textured surface  
- A shaped aiming reference such as a bead, dot, post, ring, chevron, or notch-alignment marker  

The non-opaque construction allows the user to maintain visual awareness of the target area while still perceiving a distinct aiming reference.

#### 2. Opaque Mounting Body  
The mounting body is substantially opaque and may be made from metal, polymer, composite, ceramic, or another rigid material. Suitable materials include aluminum, steel, titanium, reinforced polymer, molded thermoplastic, or metal-injection-molded alloys.

The opaque mounting body may perform several functions:

- Structurally supporting the reticle element  
- Reducing glare or unwanted light transmission  
- Shielding portions of the reticle element from stray light  
- Defining the apparent outline of the illuminated aiming mark  
- Protecting the reticle element from side impact or abrasion  
- Providing attachment features for coupling the sight assembly to a weapon, rail, slide, barrel, riser, mount, or sight base  

The mounting body may be blackened, anodized, coated, textured, matte-finished, or otherwise treated to reduce reflection.

#### 3. Channel-Based Attachment Interface  
A secure channel-based attachment interface mechanically couples the reticle element to the mounting body. The interface may include a channel formed in the opaque mounting body and configured to receive a corresponding portion of the reticle element.

The channel may be configured as:

- A longitudinal slot  
- A transverse slot  
- A dovetail channel  
- A T-slot  
- A C-shaped retaining channel  
- A blind pocket  
- A keyed groove  
- A stepped recess  
- A tapered or wedged channel  
- A press-fit, snap-fit, or adhesive-assisted retention channel  

The interface may include retention structures such as lips, shoulders, detents, tabs, pins, fasteners, staking regions, crimped portions, adhesive reservoirs, or overmolded retention surfaces. The channel arrangement may prevent one or more of upward, lateral, forward, rearward, rotational, or axial movement of the reticle element relative to the mounting body.

### Illumination Features  
The illuminated open sight assembly may be passive, active, or hybrid.

In passive embodiments, the reticle element may collect ambient light through an exposed upper or side surface and transmit the collected light to a visible aiming region. The reticle element may function as a light pipe or fiber-optic collector.

In active embodiments, an illumination source such as an LED may be optically coupled to the reticle element. A power source, control circuit, switch, brightness control, motion sensor, or automatic light sensor may be incorporated into the mounting body or a connected sight base.

In self-luminous embodiments, the reticle element may include tritium, phosphorescent material, fluorescent material, or photoluminescent pigment. The opaque mounting body may mask portions of the light source to improve aiming-mark definition.

The illuminated aiming reference may appear as a bright dot, bead, line, halo, ring, chevron, or other reticle geometry when viewed from the user’s sighting position.

### Secure Mounting and Retention  
The channel-based attachment interface is designed to improve durability relative to surface-bonded or exposed illuminated inserts. By seating the reticle element in a channel, the mounting body can provide mechanical capture along multiple sides of the reticle element. This may reduce reliance on adhesive alone and improve resistance to recoil and environmental forces.

In certain embodiments:

- The reticle element is inserted into the channel from an end of the mounting body.  
- The channel includes an undercut that prevents vertical withdrawal of the reticle element.  
- A locking member prevents longitudinal sliding after insertion.  
- Adhesive is disposed within the channel to damp vibration and seal the interface.  
- The reticle element includes a keyed profile corresponding to the channel geometry.  
- The opaque body partially surrounds the reticle element while leaving an illuminated aiming surface exposed.  
- A cover, cap, stake, pin, or crimped region secures the reticle element after installation.  

### Example Embodiment  
In one representative embodiment, an illuminated front sight includes an opaque sight body having a lower portion configured for attachment to a firearm slide or sight base and an upper portion defining a reticle-receiving channel. The channel includes opposed sidewalls and inwardly projecting lips forming an undercut profile. A translucent reticle element is slidably received within the channel and includes a complementary base profile captured beneath the lips.

An upper portion of the reticle element remains exposed to collect ambient light, while a rear-facing portion defines a visible illuminated aiming dot. The opaque body blocks side glare and frames the dot for improved contrast. A locking pin, adhesive, or deformed retaining feature prevents the reticle element from sliding out of the channel. The resulting assembly provides an illuminated aiming reference while maintaining rugged mechanical retention.

### Potential Advantages  
The disclosed sight assembly may provide one or more of the following advantages:

- Improved sight acquisition in low-light or mixed-light environments  
- Reduced target obstruction due to the non-opaque reticle element  
- Enhanced aiming-mark contrast through opaque framing and light masking  
- Improved durability under recoil, vibration, impact, and handling  
- Reduced dependence on adhesive-only retention  
- Modular replacement or customization of the reticle element  
- Compatibility with passive, active, or self-luminous illumination systems  
- Protection of the reticle element by surrounding opaque body structures  
- Secure mechanical capture through a channel-based interface  
- Adaptability to front sights, rear sights, backup sights, and modular open sight platforms  

### Representative Claim Concepts  
1. An illuminated open sight assembly comprising an opaque mounting body defining a channel and a non-opaque reticle element received at least partially within the channel, the reticle element being configured to provide an illuminated aiming reference.

2. The sight assembly wherein the channel includes retention surfaces that mechanically capture the reticle element against removal in at least one direction.

3. The sight assembly wherein the reticle element is transparent or translucent and includes a light-emitting aiming region visible to a user.

4. The sight assembly wherein the opaque mounting body masks a portion of the reticle element to define or enhance the illuminated aiming reference.

5. The sight assembly wherein the channel comprises a dovetail, T-slot, undercut slot, keyed groove, or stepped recess.

6. The sight assembly further comprising a locking member, adhesive, crimp, stake, detent, or pin configured to retain the reticle element within the channel.

7. The sight assembly wherein illumination is provided by ambient light collected by the reticle element, a fiber-optic structure, photoluminescent material, tritium, or an electrically powered light source.

8. The sight assembly wherein the opaque mounting body includes a weapon-mounting interface for attachment to a firearm slide, rail, barrel, receiver, bow, or sight base.

### Abstract-Style Summary  
An illuminated open sight assembly includes an opaque mounting body and a non-opaque reticle element secured thereto. The mounting body defines a channel configured to receive and mechanically retain at least a portion of the reticle element. The reticle element is transparent, translucent, light-guiding, fluorescent, photoluminescent, or otherwise non-opaque and provides an illuminated aiming reference visible to a user. The opaque mounting body supports the reticle element, blocks stray light, frames the aiming reference, and protects the reticle element from impact. The channel-based attachment interface may include undercuts, shoulders, dovetail surfaces, lips, locking members, adhesive, or other retention features to resist displacement during recoil, vibration, or handling. The assembly provides a durable illuminated open sight with improved visibility and secure reticle retention.
